failure_summary.description: The answer included the requested value but added cue nouns or unnecessary contextual qualifiers instead of giving only the requested slot.
The agent chose a nearby city or genre despite existing instructions to follow the clue’s intended target and use supporting context.

patch.reasoning: Most failures came from expanding an otherwise relevant answer with words that restated the clue or came only from context. A final slot-only check makes the existing minimal-answer guidance more operational. The two wrong-target cases are already covered by the evidence and target rules, so they do not warrant duplicating those rules.

edits.content: For cloze-like or elliptical prompts, make a final slot-only check: return the missing name, value, or category, not a fuller phrase that repeats the clue’s subject or adds contextual qualifiers. When wording such as “this [category]” or “nicknamed this” supplies the head noun, give only the distinguishing answer; when a place or officeholder cue asks for an associated jurisdiction, give the jurisdiction alone. Retain extra words only when they are part of the conventional answer or needed to disambiguate it.
